agility = the ability to change direction quickly and under control
coordination = the ability to use different parts of the body together smoothly
flexibility = how far your joints and muscles can stretch
recovery = the process of the body repairing itself after training
overtraining = training so hard or so often that performance and health get worse
carbohydrate loading = eating extra carbohydrates before a long event to store energy
energy drink = a drink with caffeine and sugar, marketed to boost alertness or performance
hydration = keeping enough fluid in the body during exercise
tapering = reducing training load shortly before a competition so you arrive fresh
cross-training = doing a different sport to support your main one and reduce injury
personal trainer = a coach who designs and supervises exercise for an individual
training camp = a period when athletes live and train together, often away from home
pre-season = the training period before the competitive season starts
off-season = the period when there is no official competition
peak fitness = the highest level of condition an athlete can reach for a target event
blood doping = illegally boosting performance by manipulating blood or red cells
doping = using banned substances or methods to improve sporting results
match-fixing = illegally arranging the result or events of a match, often for betting
equal pay in sport = the principle that women and men should receive comparable pay and prizes
sportsmanship = fair, respectful behaviour towards opponents and officials
